blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The beneficial effect of ustekinumab on clinical response, mucosal healing and clinical remission was observed in induction and in maintenance both in patients who failed conventional therapy but not a biologic therapy, as well as in those who had failed at least one prior TNFα antagonist therapy including in patients with a primary non-response to TNFα antagonist therapy. A beneficial effect was also observed in induction in patients who failed at least one prior TNFα antagonist therapy and vedolizumab, however the number of patients in this subgroup was too small to draw definitive conclusions about the beneficial effect in this group during maintenance.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Week 16 Responders to Ustekinumab Induction
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Ustekinumab treated patients who were not in response at week 8 of UNIFI-I received an administration of 90 mg SC ustekinumab at week 8 (36% of patients). Of those patients, 9% of patients who were initially randomised to the recommended induction dose achieved clinical remission and 58% achieved clinical response at Week 16.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Patients who were not in clinical response to ustekinumab induction at week 8 of the UNFI-I study but were in response at week 16 (157 patients) entered into the non-randomised portion of UNIFI-M and continued to receive maintenance dosing every 8 weeks; among these patients, a majority (62%) maintained response and 30% achieved remission at week 44.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Study Extension
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In UNIFI, patients who completed the study through week 44 were eligible to continue treatment in a study extension. Among the 400 patients who entered on and were treated with ustekinumab every 12 or 8 weeks in the study extension, symptomatic remission was generally maintained through week 200 for patients who failed conventional therapy (but not a biologic therapy) and those who failed biologic therapy, including those who failed both anti-TNF and vedolizumab. Among patients who received 4 years of ustekinumab treatment and were assessed using the full Mayo score at maintenance week 200, 74.2% (69/93) and 68.3% (41/60) maintained mucosal healing and clinical remission, respectively.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety analysis including 457 patients (1289.9 person-years) followed up to 220 weeks showed a safety profile between week 44 and 220 that was comparable with that observed up to week 44.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: No new safety concerns were identified in this study extension with up to 4 years of treatment in patients with ulcerative colitis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Endoscopic Normalisation
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Endoscopic normalisation was defined as a Mayo endoscopic subscore of 0 and was observed as early as week 8 of UNIFI-I. At week 44 of UNIFI-M, it was achieved in 24% and 29% of patients treated with ustekinumab every 12 or 8 weeks, respectively, as compared to 18% of patients in the placebo group.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Histologic & Histo-Endoscopic Mucosal Healing
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Histologic healing (defined as neutrophil infiltration in < 5% of crypts, no crypt destruction, and no erosions, ulcerations, or granulation tissue) was assessed at week 8 of UNIFI-I and Week 44 of UNIFI-M. At week 8, after a single intravenous induction dose, significantly greater proportions of patients in the recommended dose group achieved histologic healing (36%) compared with patients in the placebo group (22%). At Week 44 maintenance of this effect was observed with significantly more patients in histologic healing in the every 12 week (54%) and every 8 week (59%) ustekinumab groups as compared to placebo (33%).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: A combined endpoint of histo-endoscopic mucosal healing defined as subjects having both mucosal healing and histologic healing was evaluated at week 8 of UNIFI-I and week 44 of UNIFI-M. Patients receiving ustekinumab at the recommended dose showed significant improvements on the histoendoscopic mucosal healing endpoint at week 8 in the ustekinumab group (18%) as compared to the placebo group (9%). At week 44, maintenance of this effect was observed with significantly more patients in histo-endoscopic mucosal healing in the every 12 week (39%) and every 8 week (46%) ustekinumab groups as compared to placebo (24%).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Health-related quality of life
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Health-related quality of life was assessed by Inflammatory Bowel Disease Questionnaire (IBDQ), SF-36 and EuroQoL-5D (EQ-5D) questionnaires.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: At week 8 of UNIFI-I, patients receiving ustekinumab showed significantly greater and clinically meaningful improvements on IBDQ total score, EQ-5D and EQ-5D VAS, and SF-36 Mental Component Summary Score and SF-36 Physical Component Summary Score when compared to placebo. These improvements were maintained in ustekinumab-treated patients in UNIFI-M through week 44. Improvement in health-related quality of life as measured by IBDQ and SF-36 was generally maintained during the extension through week 200.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Patients receiving ustekinumab experienced significantly more improvements in work productivity as assessed by greater reductions in overall work impairment and in activity impairment as assessed by the WPAI-GH questionnaire than patients receiving placebo.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Hospitalisations and ulcerative colitis (UC) related surgeries
section_path: Hospitalisations and ulcerative colitis (UC) related surgeries
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Through week 8 of UNIFI-I, the proportions of subjects with UC disease related hospitalisations were significantly lower for subjects in the ustekinumab recommended dose group (1.6%, 5/322) compared with subjects in the placebo group (4.4%, 14/319) and no subjects underwent UC disease related surgeries in subjects receiving ustekinumab at the recommended induction dose compared to 0.6% (2/319) subjects in the placebo group.
section_path: Hospitalisations and ulcerative colitis (UC) related surgeries
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Through week 44 of UNIFI-M, a significantly lower number of UC-related hospitalisations was observed in subjects in the combined ustekinumab group (2.0%, 7/348) as compared with subjects in the placebo group (5.7%, 10/175). A numerically lower number of subjects in the ustekinumab group (0.6%, 2/348) underwent UC disease related surgeries compared with subjects in the placebo group (1.7%, 3/175) through week 44.
section_path: Hospitalisations and ulcerative colitis (UC) related surgeries
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Immunogenicity
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Antibodies to ustekinumab may develop during ustekinumab treatment and most are neutralising. The formation of anti-ustekinumab antibodies is associated with both increased clearance and reduced efficacy of ustekinumab, except in patients with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis where no reduced efficacy was observed. There is no apparent correlation between the presence of anti-ustekinumab antibodies and the occurrence of injection site reactions.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Paediatric population
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The European Medicines Agency has deferred the obligation to submit the results of studies with ustekinumab in one or more subsets of the paediatric population in Crohn's Disease and ulcerative colitis. The pre-filled pen has not been studied in the paediatric population and is not recommended for use by paediatric patients.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.2 Pharmacokinetic properties
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Absorption
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The median time to reach the maximum serum concentration (tmax) was 8.5 days after a single 90 mg subcutaneous administration in healthy subjects. The median tmax values of ustekinumab following a single subcutaneous administration of either 45 mg or 90 mg in patients with psoriasis were comparable to those observed in healthy subjects.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The absolute bioavailability of ustekinumab following a single subcutaneous administration was estimated to be 57.2% in patients with psoriasis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Distribution
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Median volume of distribution during the terminal phase (Vz) following a single intravenous administration to patients with psoriasis ranged from 57 to 83 mL/kg.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Biotransformation
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The exact metabolic pathway for ustekinumab is unknown.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Elimination
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Median systemic clearance (CL) following a single intravenous administration to patients with psoriasis ranged from 1.99 to 2.34 mL/day/kg. Median half-life (t1/2) of ustekinumab was approximately 3 weeks in patients with psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, ranging from 15 to 32 days across all psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis studies. In a population pharmacokinetic analysis, the apparent clearance (CL/F) and apparent volume of distribution (V/F) were 0.465 l/day and 15.7 l, respectively, in patients with psoriasis. The CL/F of ustekinumab was not impacted by gender. Population pharmacokinetic analysis showed that there was a trend towards a higher clearance of ustekinumab in patients who tested positive for antibodies to ustekinumab.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Dose linearity
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The systemic exposure of ustekinumab (Cmax and AUC) increased in an approximately dose-proportional manner after a single intravenous administration at doses ranging from 0.09 mg/kg to 4.5 mg/kg or following a single subcutaneous administration at doses ranging from approximately 24 mg to 240 mg in patients with psoriasis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Single dose versus multiple doses
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Serum concentration-time profiles of ustekinumab were generally predictable after single or multiple subcutaneous dose administrations. In patients with psoriasis, steady-state serum concentrations of ustekinumab were achieved by week 28 after initial subcutaneous doses at Weeks 0 and 4 followed by doses every 12 weeks. The median steady-state trough concentration ranged from 0.21 μg/mL to 0.26 μg/mL (45 mg) and from 0.47 μg/mL to 0.49 μg/mL (90 mg). There was no apparent accumulation in serum ustekinumab concentration over time when given subcutaneously every 12 weeks.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In patients with Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, following an intravenous dose of ~6 mg/kg, starting at week 8, subcutaneous maintenance dosing of 90 mg ustekinumab was administered every 8 or 12 weeks. Steady state ustekinumab concentration was achieved by the start of the second maintenance dose. In patients with Crohn's disease, median steady-state trough concentrations ranged from 1.97 μg/mL to 2.24 μg/mL and from 0.61 μg/mL to 0.76 μg/mL for 90 mg ustekinumab every 8 weeks or every 12 weeks respectively. In patients with ulcerative colitis, median steady-state trough concentrations ranged from 2.69 μg/mL to 3.09 μg/mL and from 0.92 μg/mL to 1.19 μg/mL for 90 mg ustekinumab every 8 weeks or every 12 weeks. The steady-state trough ustekinumab levels resulting from 90 mg ustekinumab every 8 weeks were associated with higher clinical remission rates as compared to the steady-state trough levels following 90 mg every 12 weeks.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Impact of weight on pharmacokinetics
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In a population pharmacokinetic analysis using data from patients with psoriasis, body weight was found to be the most significant covariate affecting the clearance of ustekinumab. The median CL/F in patients with weight > 100 kg was approximately 55% higher compared to patients with weight ≤ 100 kg. The median V/F in patients with weight > 100 kg was approximately 37% higher as compared to patients with weight ≤ 100 kg. The median trough serum concentrations of ustekinumab in patients with higher weight (> 100 kg) in the 90 mg group were comparable to those in patients with lower weight (≤ 100 kg) in the 45 mg group. Similar results were obtained from a confirmatory population pharmacokinetic analysis using data from patients with psoriatic arthritis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Dosing frequency adjustment
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In patients with Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, based on observed data and population PK analyses, randomised subjects who lost response to treatment had lower serum ustekinumab concentrations over time compared with subjects who did not lose response. In Crohn's disease, dose adjustment from 90 mg every 12 weeks to 90 mg every 8 weeks was associated with an increase in trough serum ustekinumab concentrations and an accompanying increase in efficacy. In ulcerative colitis, population PK model based simulations demonstrated that adjusting dosing from 90 mg every 12 weeks to every 8 weeks would be expected to result in a 3-fold increase in steady-state trough ustekinumab concentrations. Additionally on the basis of clinical trial data in patients with ulcerative colitis, a positive exposure-response relationship was established between trough concentrations, and clinical remission and mucosal healing.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Special populations
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: No pharmacokinetic data are available in patients with impaired renal or hepatic function. No specific studies have been conducted in elderly patients.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The pharmacokinetics of ustekinumab were generally comparable between Asian and non-Asian patients with psoriasis and ulcerative colitis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In patients with Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, variability in ustekinumab clearance was affected by body weight, serum albumin level, sex, and antibody to ustekinumab status while body weight was the main covariate affecting the volume of distribution. Additionally in Crohn's disease, clearance was affected by C-reactive protein, TNF antagonist failure status and race (Asian versus non-Asian). The impact of these covariates was within ±20% of the typical or reference value of the respective PK parameter, thus dose adjustment is not warranted for these covariates. Concomitant use of immunomodulators did not have a significant impact on ustekinumab disposition.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In the population pharmacokinetic analysis, there were no indications of an effect of tobacco or alcohol on the pharmacokinetics of ustekinumab.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The bioavailability of ustekinumab following administration by syringe or pre-filled pen was comparable.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The pre-filled pen has not been studied in the paediatric population and is not recommended for use by paediatric patients.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Regulation of CYP450 enzymes
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The effects of IL-12 or IL-23 on the regulation of CYP450 enzymes were evaluated in an in vitro study using human hepatocytes, which showed that IL-12 and/or IL-23 at levels of 10 ng/mL did not alter human CYP450 enzyme activities (CYP1A2, 2B6, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, or 3A4; see section 4.5).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: A phase 1, open-label, drug interaction study, Study CNTO1275CRD1003, was conducted to evaluate the effect of ustekinumab on cytochrome P450 enzyme activities following induction and maintenance dosing in patients with active Crohn's disease (n=18). No clinically significant changes in exposure of caffeine (CYP1A2 substrate), warfarin (CYP2C9 substrate), omeprazole (CYP2C19 substrate), dextromethorphan (CYP2D6 substrate), or midazolam (CYP3A substrate) were observed when used concomitantly with ustekinumab at the approved recommended dosing in patients with Crohn's disease (see section 4.5).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.3 Preclinical safety data
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Non-clinical data reveal no special hazard (e.g. organ toxicity) for humans based on studies of repeated-dose toxicity and developmental and reproductive toxicity, including safety pharmacology evaluations. In developmental and reproductive toxicity studies in cynomolgus monkeys, neither adverse effects on male fertility indices nor birth defects or developmental toxicity were observed. No adverse effects on female fertility indices were observed using an analogous antibody to IL-12/23 in mice.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Dose levels in animal studies were up to approximately 45-fold higher than the highest equivalent dose intended to be administered to psoriasis patients and resulted in peak serum concentrations in monkeys that were more than 100-fold higher than observed in humans.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Carcinogenicity studies were not performed with ustekinumab due to the lack of appropriate models for an antibody with no cross-reactivity to rodent IL-12/23 p40.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 6.6 Special precautions for disposal and other handling
section_path: 6.6 Special precautions for disposal and other handling
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The solution in the Steqeyma pre-filled pen should not be shaken. The solution should be visually inspected for particulate matter or discolouration prior to subcutaneous administration. The solution is clear to slightly opalescent, colourless to pale yellow and may contain a few small translucent or white particles of protein. This appearance is not unusual for proteinaceous solutions. The medicinal product should not be used if the solution is discoloured or cloudy, or if foreign particulate matter is present. Before administration, Steqeyma should be allowed to reach room temperature (approximately half an hour). Detailed instructions for administration are provided in the package leaflet.
section_path: 6.6 Special precautions for disposal and other handling
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma does not contain preservatives; therefore any unused medicinal product remaining in the pre-filled pen should not be used. Steqeyma is supplied as a sterile, single-use pre-filled pen. The prefilled pen must never be re-used. Any unused medicinal product or waste material should be disposed of in accordance with local requirements.

blocks.text: 1. What Steqeyma is and what it is used for
section_path: 1. What Steqeyma is and what it is used for
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: What Steqeyma is
section_path: 1. What Steqeyma is and what it is used for
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma contains the active substance 'ustekinumab', a monoclonal antibody. Monoclonal antibodies are proteins that recognise and bind specifically to certain proteins in the body.
section_path: 1. What Steqeyma is and what it is used for
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma belongs to a group of medicines called 'immunosuppressants'. These medicines work by weakening part of the immune system.
section_path: 1. What Steqeyma is and what it is used for
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: What Steqeyma is used for
section_path: 1. What Steqeyma is and what it is used for
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma is used to treat the following inflammatory diseases:
section_path: 1. What Steqeyma is and what it is used for
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Moderate to severe Crohn's disease - in adults and children who weigh at least 40 kg
section_path: 1. What Steqeyma is and what it is used for
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Moderate to severe ulcerative colitis - in adults
section_path: 1. What Steqeyma is and what it is used for
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Crohn's disease
section_path: 1. What Steqeyma is and what it is used for
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Crohn's disease is an inflammatory disease of the bowel. If you have Crohn's disease you will first be given other medicines. If you do not respond well enough or are intolerant to these medicines, you may be given Steqeyma to reduce the signs and symptoms of your disease.
section_path: 1. What Steqeyma is and what it is used for
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Ulcerative colitis
section_path: 1. What Steqeyma is and what it is used for
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Ulcerative colitis is an inflammatory disease of the bowel. If you have ulcerative colitis you will first be given other medicines. If you do not respond well enough or are intolerant to these medicines, you may be given Steqeyma to reduce the signs and symptoms of your disease.
section_path: 1. What Steqeyma is and what it is used for
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Do not use Steqeyma
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you are allergic to ustekinumab or any of the other ingredients of this medicine (listed in section 6).
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you have an active infection which your doctor thinks is important.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If you are not sure if any of the above applies to you, talk to your doctor or pharmacist before using Steqeyma.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Warnings and precautions
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before using Steqeyma. Your doctor will check how well you are before treatment. Make sure you tell your doctor about any illness you have before treatment. Also tell your doctor if you have recently been near anyone who might have tuberculosis. Your doctor will examine you and do a test for tuberculosis, before you have Steqeyma. If your doctor thinks you are at risk of tuberculosis, you may be given medicines to treat it.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Look out for serious side effects
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
Look out for serious side effects
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma can cause serious side effects, including allergic reactions and infections. You must look out for certain signs of illness while you are taking Steqeyma. See 'Serious side effects' in section 4 for a full list of these side effects.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
Look out for serious side effects
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Before you use Steqeyma tell your doctor:
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
Before you use Steqeyma tell your doctor:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you ever had an allergic reaction to ustekinumab. Ask your doctor if you are not sure.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
Before you use Steqeyma tell your doctor:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you have ever had any type of cancer - this is because immunosuppressants like Steqeyma weaken part of the immune system. This may increase the risk of cancer.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
Before you use Steqeyma tell your doctor:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you have been treated for psoriasis with other biologic medicines (a medicine produced from a biological source and usually given by injection) - the risk of cancer may be higher.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
Before you use Steqeyma tell your doctor:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you have or have had a recent infection or if you have any abnormal skin openings (fistulae).
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
Before you use Steqeyma tell your doctor:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you have any new or changing lesions within psoriasis areas or on normal skin.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
Before you use Steqeyma tell your doctor:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you are having any other treatment for psoriasis and/or psoriatic arthritis - such as another immunosuppressant or phototherapy (when your body is treated with a type of ultraviolet (UV) light). These treatments may also weaken part of the immune system. Using these therapies together with ustekinumab has not been studied. However it is possible it may increase the chance of diseases related to a weaker immune system.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
Before you use Steqeyma tell your doctor:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you are having or have ever had injections to treat allergies - it is not known if ustekinumab may affect these.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
Before you use Steqeyma tell your doctor:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you are 65 years of age or over - you may be more likely to get infections.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
Before you use Steqeyma tell your doctor:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If you are not sure if any of the above applies to you, talk to your doctor or pharmacist before using Steqeyma.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
Before you use Steqeyma tell your doctor:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Some patients have experienced lupus-like reactions including skin lupus or lupus-like syndrome during treatment with ustekinumab. Talk to your doctor right away if you experience a red, raised, scaly rash sometimes with a darker border, in areas of the skin that are exposed to the sun or with joint pains.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
Before you use Steqeyma tell your doctor:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Heart attack and strokes
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Heart attack and strokes have been observed in a study in patients with psoriasis treated with ustekinumab. Your doctor will regularly check your risk factors for heart disease and stroke in order to ensure that they are appropriately treated. Seek medical attention right away if you develop chest pain, weakness or abnormal sensation on one side of your body, facial droop, or speech or visual abnormalities.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Children and adolescents
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma is not recommended for use in children who weigh less than 40 kg with Crohn's disease or children under 18 years of age with ulcerative colitis because it has not been studied in this age group.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Other medicines, vaccines and Steqeyma
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Tell your doctor or pharmacist:
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you are taking, have recently taken or might take any other medicines.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you have recently had or are going to have a vaccination. Some types of vaccines (live vaccines) should not be given while using Steqeyma.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you received Steqeyma while pregnant, tell your baby's doctor about your Steqeyma treatment before the baby receives any vaccine, including live vaccines, such as the BCG vaccine (used to prevent tuberculosis). Live vaccines are not recommended for your baby in the first twelve months after birth if you received Steqeyma during the pregnancy unless your baby's doctor recommends otherwise.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Pregnancy and breast-feeding
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or are planning to have a baby, ask your doctor for advice before taking this medicine.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  A higher risk of birth defects has not been seen in babies exposed to ustekinumab in the womb. However, there is limited experience with ustekinumab in pregnant women. It is therefore preferable to avoid the use of Steqeyma in pregnancy.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you are a woman of childbearing potential, you are advised to avoid becoming pregnant and must use adequate contraception while using Steqeyma and for at least 15 weeks after the last Steqeyma treatment.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Ustekinumab can pass across the placenta to the unborn baby. If you received Steqeyma during your pregnancy, your baby may have a higher risk for getting an infection.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  It is important that you tell your baby's doctors and other health care professionals if you received Steqeyma during your pregnancy before the baby receives any vaccine. Live vaccines such as the BCG vaccine (used to prevent tuberculosis) are not recommended for your baby in the first twelve months after birth if you received Steqeyma during the pregnancy unless your baby's doctor recommends otherwise.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Ustekinumab may pass into breast milk in very small amounts. Talk to your doctor if you are breast-feeding or are planning to breast-feed. You and your doctor should decide if you should breast-feed or use Steqeyma - do not do both.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Driving and using machines
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma has no or negligible influence on the ability to drive and use machines.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Steqeyma contains sodium
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma contains less than 1 mmol sodium (23 mg) per dose, that is to say essentially 'sodium-free'. However, before Steqeyma is given to you, it is mixed with a solution that contains sodium. Talk to your doctor if you are on a low salt diet.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Steqeyma contains polysorbate 80
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma contains 10.37 mg of polysorbate 80 (E433) in each dosage unit which is equivalent to 0.40 mg/mL. Polysorbates may cause allergic reactions. Tell your doctor if you have any known allergies.
section_path: 2. What you need to know before you use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 3. How Steqeyma will be given
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma is intended for use under the guidance and supervision of a doctor experienced in the diagnosis and treatment of Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma 130 mg concentrate for solution for infusion will be given to you by your doctor, through a drip in the vein of your arm (intravenous infusion) over at least one hour. Talk to your doctor about when you will have your injections and follow-up appointments.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: How much Steqeyma is given
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Your doctor will decide how much Steqeyma you need to receive and for how long.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Adults aged 18 years or older
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  The doctor will work out the recommended intravenous infusion dose for you based on your body weight.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  After the starting intravenous dose, you will have the next dose of 90 mg Steqeyma by an injection under your skin (subcutaneous injection) 8 weeks later, and then every 12 weeks thereafter.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Children with Crohn's disease who weigh at least 40 kg
section_path: Children with Crohn's disease who weigh at least 40 kg
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  The doctor will work out the recommended intravenous infusion dose for you based on your body weight.
section_path: Children with Crohn's disease who weigh at least 40 kg
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  After the starting intravenous dose, you will have the next dose of 90 mg Steqeyma by an injection under your skin (subcutaneous injection) 8 weeks later, and then every 12 weeks thereafter.
section_path: Children with Crohn's disease who weigh at least 40 kg
blocks.speaker: label

section_path: Children with Crohn's disease who weigh at least 40 kg

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: How Steqeyma is given
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  The first dose of Steqeyma for treatment of Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis is given by a doctor as a drip in the vein of an arm (intravenous infusion).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Talk to your doctor if you have any questions about receiving Steqeyma.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: If you forget to use Steqeyma
section_path: If you forget to use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If you forget or miss the appointment for receiving the dose, contact your doctor to reschedule your appointment.
section_path: If you forget to use Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: If you stop using Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: It is not dangerous to stop using Steqeyma. However, if you stop, your symptoms may come back.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If you have any further questions on the use of this medicine, ask your doctor or pharmacist.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 4. Possible side effects
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Like all medicines, this medicine can cause side effects, although not everybody gets them.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Serious side effects
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Some patients may have serious side effects that may need urgent treatment.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Allergic reactions - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor or get emergency medical help straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
section_path: Allergic reactions - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor or get emergency medical help straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Serious allergic reactions ('anaphylaxis') are rare in people taking ustekinumab (may affect up to 1 in 1 000 people). Signs include:
section_path: Allergic reactions - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor or get emergency medical help straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: difficulty breathing or swallowing
section_path: Allergic reactions - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor or get emergency medical help straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: low blood pressure, which can cause dizziness or light-headedness
section_path: Allergic reactions - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor or get emergency medical help straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: swelling of the face, lips, mouth or throat.
section_path: Allergic reactions - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor or get emergency medical help straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Common signs of an allergic reaction include skin rash and hives (these may affect up to 1 in 100 people).
section_path: Allergic reactions - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor or get emergency medical help straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Infusion-related reactions - If you are being treated for Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, the first dose of Steqeyma is given through a drip into a vein (intravenous infusion). Some patients have experienced serious allergic reactions during the infusion.
section_path: Allergic reactions - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor or get emergency medical help straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In rare cases, allergic lung reactions and lung inflammation have been reported in patients who receive ustekinumab. Tell your doctor right away if you develop symptoms such as cough, shortness of breath, and fever.
section_path: Allergic reactions - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor or get emergency medical help straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If you have a serious allergic reaction, your doctor may decide that you should not use Steqeyma again.
section_path: Allergic reactions - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor or get emergency medical help straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Infections of the nose or throat and common cold are common (may affect up to 1 in 10 people)
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Infections of the chest are uncommon (may affect up to 1 in 100 people)
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Inflammation of tissue under the skin ('cellulitis') is uncommon (may affect up to 1 in 100 people)
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Shingles (a type of painful rash with blisters) are uncommon (may affect up to 1 in 100 people)
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma may make you less able to fight infections. Some infections could become serious and may include infections caused by viruses, fungi, bacteria (including tuberculosis), or parasites, including infections that mainly occur in people with a weakened immune system (opportunistic infections). Opportunistic infections of the brain (encephalitis, meningitis), lungs, and eye have been reported in patients receiving treatment with ustekinumab.
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: You must look out for signs of infection while you are using Steqeyma. These include:
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  fever, flu-like symptoms, night sweats, weight loss
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  feeling tired or short of breath; cough which will not go away
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  warm, red and painful skin, or a painful skin rash with blisters
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  burning when passing water
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  diarrhoea
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  visual disturbance or vision loss
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  headache, neck stiffness, light sensitivity, nausea or confusion.
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of these signs of infection. These may be signs of infections such as chest infections, skin infections, shingles or opportunistic infections that could have serious complications. Tell your doctor if you have any kind of infection that will not go away or keeps coming back. Your doctor may decide that you should not use Steqeyma until the infection goes away. Also tell your doctor if you have any open cuts or sores as they might get infected.
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Shedding of skin - increase in redness and shedding of skin over a larger area of the body may be symptoms of erythrodermic psoriasis or exfoliative dermatitis, which are serious skin conditions. You should tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of these signs.
section_path: Infections - these may need urgent treatment. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice any of the following signs.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.text: Reporting of side effects

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If you get any side effects, talk to your doctor or pharmacist. This includes any possible side effects not listed in this leaflet. You can also report side effects directly via the national reporting system listed in Appendix V. By reporting side effects you can help provide more information on the safety of this medicine.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5. How to store Steqeyma
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Steqeyma 130 mg concentrate for solution for infusion is given in a hospital or clinic and patients should not need to store or handle it.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Keep this medicine out of the sight and reach of children.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Store in a refrigerator (2 °C-8 °C). Do not freeze.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Keep the vial in the outer carton in order to protect from light.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If needed, individual Steqeyma vials may also be stored at room temperature up to 25 °C for a maximum single period of up to 31 days in the original carton in order to protect from light. Record the date when the vial is first removed from the refrigerator in the space provided on the outer carton. At any time before the end of this 31-day period at room temperature, the product can be returned to the refrigerator once, and stored there until the original expiry date. Discard the vial if not used within 31 days at room temperature storage or by the original expiry date, whichever is earlier.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not shake the Steqeyma vials. Prolonged vigorous shaking may damage the medicine.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Do not use this medicine:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  After the expiry date which is stated on the label and the carton after 'EXP'. The expiry date refers to the last day of that month.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If the liquid is discoloured, cloudy or you can see other foreign particles floating in it (see section 6 'What Steqeyma looks like and contents of the pack').
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you know, or think that it may have been exposed to extreme temperatures (such as accidentally frozen or heated).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If the product has been shaken vigorously.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If the seal is broken.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma is for single use only. Any diluted infusion solution or unused product remaining in the vial and the syringe should be thrown away in accordance with local requirements.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Instructions for dilution:
section_path: 6. Contents of the pack and other information
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Steqeyma concentrate for solution for infusion must be diluted, prepared and infused by a healthcare professional using aseptic technique.
section_path: 6. Contents of the pack and other information
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Calculate the dose and the number of Steqeyma vials needed based on patient weight (see section 3, Table 1, Table 2). Each 26 mL vial of Steqeyma contains 130 mg of ustekinumab.
section_path: 6. Contents of the pack and other information
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Withdraw and then discard a volume of the sodium chloride 9 mg/mL (0.9%) solution from the 250 mL infusion bag equal to the volume of Steqeyma to be added (discard 26 mL sodium chloride for each vial of Steqeyma needed, for 2 vials - discard 52 mL, for 3 vials - discard 78 mL, for 4 vials - discard 104 mL).
section_path: 6. Contents of the pack and other information
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Withdraw 26 mL of Steqeyma from each vial needed and add it to the 250 mL infusion bag. The final volume in the infusion bag should be 250 mL. Gently mix.
section_path: 6. Contents of the pack and other information
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Visually inspect the diluted solution before infusion. Do not use if visibly opaque particles, discolouration or foreign particles are observed.
section_path: 6. Contents of the pack and other information
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Infuse the diluted solution over a period of at least one hour. Once diluted, the infusion should be completed within forty-eight hours of the dilution in the infusion bag.
section_path: 6. Contents of the pack and other information
